To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oscillatory activity observed in area 17 is of synaptic origin and that the frequency of oscillations depends on the configuration of the visual input.
the rhythmic patterns in neuronal output observed in 28 % of cells of area 17 of the kitten visual cortex originate in the periodicity of synaptic inputs.
oscillatory activity in kitten area-17 neurones is a manifestation of periodic synaptic input, and is not generated intrinsically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the generation of rhythmic activity in area 17.
the analysis of oscillations of neuronal membrane potential and firing activity in the visual system, with the aim of identifying the synaptic mechanisms underlying these phenomena.
the analysis of the mechanisms of visual cortical plasticity in the developing cat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rhythmicity of neuronal discharge is not an inherent property of cortical neurons, but is rather imposed by a rhythmic input.
oscillations in area 17 neuronal activity result from the summation of periodic synaptic inputs.
the oscillations observed in area 17 neurone activity are the result of a rhythmic input from thalamic neurones, and that this rhythmic input is generated in the thalamic circuitry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rhythmicity of neuronal activity is not a property of individual cells, but is rather an emergent property of the network.
the regularity in the discharge of cortical neurones, which is observed in the adult cat, has its origin in afferent activity in the immature kitten.
oscillatory behaviour of cortical neurones is a consequence of rhythmic activity of afferents, which is in turn related to the spatiotemporal characteristics of the visual input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oscillation of membrane potential at 10 Hz in area 17 neurone is the consequence of afferent activity.
the oscillatory behaviour of the cells in the visual cortex can be attributed to synaptic input, rather than to the intrinsic dynamics of the cells themselves.
the oscillations in the membrane potential are not a result of the oscillations in neuronal firing.
